searchText: <timbeiko> Thanks for sharing! Definitely need to think about this more, but a few initial thoughts: - I think we’ve tried hard to avoid committing to timelines publicly, caveating them when we do, and also having documents which explain what’s still todo (e.g. the readiness checklist). It’s a fine line between sharing progress as it’s done and also making it clear that “unknown unknowns” are very real.if we find a bad bug even 1 week before we go live, we will have to delay. Suggestions welcome about how we can communicate this better! - We have started approaching end users and applications/infra to get them to use the devnets, Kintsugi being the latest. Our “strategy” has been to try and grow the number of stakeholders involved in each iteration, but we are getting towards more stable ones where it’d be nice to see more professional use. - as for comms/PR, we currently have the Ethereum blog, where we share major updates, my blog where I share more in-progress ones, and various ad-hoc channels. Is there anything else you think we should have? More stuff on the Ethereum.org blog? <dannyryan> We’ve also done two community calls, no? with plans of more as kintsugi stablizes and we have a firmer testnet/testing plan? cross-posted from <#598292067260825641> ---------- Reminder! CL call in 26 hours https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/443 First part will be about kintsugi/the-merge. EL teams, please join us! https://sepolia.ethdevops.io/ It exists, but it's a fairly lonesome place am i at the right CL call link? going to assume no bc there's no one there Yep, the plan is for another call 🔜, but we're trying to see if any complex application has been deployed to Kintsugi first. Noob question for eth2 folks: why are integers fixed width in SSZ? What's the link for the CL call? https://ethereumfoundation.zoom.us/j/91725886939?pwd=b2kzT0JGeFAzTmhyb1BYSTgrZ0xwdz09 thank you Speculation: simplicity, and in many cases widths aren't particularly variable so there is no (or sometimes negative) savings by having variable width. A timestamp, for example, won't have a high variability in width. It does require more care with picking appropriate widths though. Also, I think you can throw a compression layer on top of SSZ and get much of the benefit of variable width encoders. And indeed we use snappy compression for communication between peers. Out of curiosity, has anyone compared compression of real-world data between SSZ + snappy vs RLP + snappy? Or something similar. I know there was some analysis done on how effective snappy compression was for typical gossip messages but not sure where that was or if anything similar has been done for RLP. I'm guessing it was done for RLP at some point because I think an eth protocol update introduced snappy compression so I'm guessing there was some evidence it actually helped.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<timbeiko> Thanks for sharing!
Definitely need to think about this more, but a few initial thoughts: 
- I think we’ve tried hard to avoid committing to timelines publicly, caveating them when we do, and also having documents which explain what’s still todo (e.g. the readiness checklist). It’s a fine line between sharing progress as it’s done and also making it clear that “unknown unknowns” are very real.if we find a bad bug even 1 week before we go live, we will have to delay. Suggestions welcome about how we can communicate this better!
- We have started approaching end users and applications/infra to get them to use the devnets, Kintsugi being the latest. Our “strategy” has been to try and grow the number of stakeholders involved in each iteration, but we are getting towards more stable ones where it’d be nice to see more professional use. 
- as for comms/PR, we currently have the Ethereum blog, where we share major updates, my blog where I share more in-progress ones, and various ad-hoc channels. Is there anything else you think we should have? More stuff on the Ethereum.org blog?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> We’ve also done two community calls, no? with plans of more as kintsugi stablizes and we have a firmer testnet/testing plan?
